# UD Pali PaliCanon

Language: [Pali](/pi/index.html) (code: `pi`)<br/>
Family: IE

This treebank has been part of Universal Dependencies since the UD v2.19 release.

The following people have contributed to making this treebank part of UD: Chia-Wei Lin, Jasvinder Singh, Khemarato Bhikkhu.

Repository: [UD_Pali-PaliCanon](https://github.com/UniversalDependencies/UD_Pali-PaliCanon)<br />
Search this treebank on-line: [PML-TQ](https://lindat.mff.cuni.cz/services/pmltq/#!/treebank/udpi_palicanon219)<br />
Download all treebanks: [UD 2.19](/#download)

License: CC BY-SA 4.0

Genre: nonfiction

Questions, comments?
General annotation questions (either Pali-specific or cross-linguistic) can be raised in the [main UD issue tracker](https://github.com/UniversalDependencies/docs/issues).
You can report bugs in this treebank in the [treebank-specific issue tracker on Github](https://github.com/UniversalDependencies/UD_Pali-PaliCanon/issues).
If you want to collaborate, please contact [khemarato&nbsp;•&nbsp;bhikkhu&nbsp;(æt)&nbsp;gmail&nbsp;•&nbsp;com].
Development of the treebank happens directly in the UD repository, so you may submit bug fixes as pull requests against the dev branch.

| Annotation | Source |
|------------|--------|
| Lemmas | annotated manually |
| UPOS | annotated manually, natively in UD style |
| XPOS | not available |
| Features | annotated manually, natively in UD style |
| Relations | annotated manually, natively in UD style |

## Description

UD_Pali-PaliCanon is the first UD-native treebank for the manual annotation of sentences from [the Pāli Canon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pali_Canon).


## Acknowledgments

We would like to thank Dibyajyoti Jana, Henrik Hornecker, and Prof. Dr. Ingo Strauch for sharing their expertise in Indic languages and linguistics, which helped us refine our UD annotation guidelines for Pāli.

<h2>Tokenization and Word Segmentation</h2>


<ul>
<li>This corpus contains 225 sentences, 1719 tokens and 2051 syntactic words.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus contains 128 tokens (7%) that are not followed by a space.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus does not contain words with spaces.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus does not contain words that contain both letters and punctuation.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus contains 274 multi-word tokens. On average, one multi-word token consists of 2.21 syntactic words.</li>
<li>There are 147 types of multi-word tokens. Examples: sammāsambuddhassa, sammāsambuddho, Kiṃpaccayā, bodhisattamātā, bhaddayugaṃ, mātukucchiṃ, sāvakayugaṃ, devānubhāvaṃ, āyuppamāṇaṃ, asītibhikkhusahassāni, bhikkhusatasahassaṃ, bodhisattamātu, jarāmaraṇaṃ, khīṇāsavānaṃ, Nāmarūpanirodhā, Nāmarūpapaccayā, Nāmarūpe, andhakāratimisā, asītivassasahassāni, aññamaññaṃ, aṭṭhasaṭṭhibhikkhusatasahassaṃ, candimasūriyā, dasasahassī, ekanavutikappe, evaṃmahiddhikā, evaṃmahānubhāvā, jarāmaraṇan, kesamassuṃ, khaṇḍatissaṃ, lokadhātu, lokantarikā, mahāpurisassa, mātukucchimhā, nāmarūpan, nāmarūpaṃ, sabrahmake, sadevake, sadevamanussāya, samārake, sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā, suppatiṭṭhitapādo, upādānakkhandhesu, uyyānabhūmiṃ, Bhavanirodhā, Bhavapaccayā, Jātinirodhā, Jātipaccayā, Khattiyakule, Parosahassaṃ, Phassanirodhā.</li>
</ul>

<h3>Other Features</h3>


<h2>Syntax</h2>

<h3>Auxiliary Verbs and Copula</h3>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 2 lemmas as copulas (<a>cop</a>). Examples: bhavati, atthi.</li>
</ul>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 1 lemmas as auxiliaries (<a>aux</a>). Examples: bhavati.</li>
</ul>

<h3>Core Arguments, Oblique Arguments and Adjuncts</h3>

Here we consider only relations between verbs (parent) and nouns or pronouns (child).
<ul>
  <li><a>nsubj</a>
    <ul>
      <li>VERB--PRON-Nom (1)</li>
      <li>VERB-Conv--NOUN-Nom (1)</li>
      <li>VERB-Fin--NOUN-Nom (88)</li>
      <li>VERB-Fin--PRON-Nom (17)</li>
      <li>VERB-Part--NOUN-Loc (12)</li>
      <li>VERB-Part--NOUN-Nom (13)</li>
      <li>VERB-Part--PRON-Gen (1)</li>
      <li>VERB-Part--PRON-Loc (10)</li>
      <li>VERB-Part--PRON-Nom (1)</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<ul>
  <li><a>obj</a>
    <ul>
      <li>VERB-Conv--NOUN-Acc (14)</li>
      <li>VERB-Fin--NOUN-Acc (16)</li>
      <li>VERB-Fin--PRON-Acc (3)</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>

<ul>
  <li><a>iobj</a>
    <ul>
    </ul>
  </li>
</ul>




<h3>Relations Overview</h3>

<ul>
<li>This corpus uses 11 relation subtypes: <a>acl:relcl</a>, <a>compound:av</a>, <a>compound:bv</a>, <a>compound:dg</a>, <a>compound:dv</a>, <a>compound:kd</a>, <a>compound:na</a>, <a>compound:tp</a>, <a>nsubj:pass</a>, <a>obl:agent</a>, <a>obl:goal</a></li>
<li>The following 1 main types are not used alone, they are always subtyped: <a>compound</a></li>
<li>The following 12 relation types are not used in this corpus at all: <a>iobj</a>, <a>csubj</a>, <a>expl</a>, <a>clf</a>, <a>case</a>, <a>fixed</a>, <a>flat</a>, <a>list</a>, <a>goeswith</a>, <a>reparandum</a>, <a>punct</a>, <a>dep</a></li>
</ul>
